eatWell.title: Eat well
eatWell.subtitle: Heart-healthy Ethiopian foods
eatWell.cardBody: A heart-healthy guide with local foods: what to eat more of, what to limit.
eatWell.recommendedIntro: Choose these regularly. A heart-healthy pattern is not a strict diet; it is what you eat most days, over time.
eatWell.limitIntro: Eat these less often. They raise blood pressure or cholesterol.

pattern.plants: Eat plenty of vegetables, fruit and whole grains.
pattern.protein: Choose legumes, nuts, seeds and fish. Have eggs and lean chicken in smaller amounts, and red meat only 1–3 times a week.
pattern.dairy: Choose unflavoured milk and yoghurt. If you have heart disease or high cholesterol, choose reduced-fat.
pattern.fats: Use healthy oils such as olive, canola or sunflower, in small amounts.
pattern.herbs: Flavour food with herbs and spices instead of salt.

wholeGrains.title: Whole grains
wholeGrains.body: High in fibre; can help lower cholesterol.

vegetables.title: Vegetables
vegetables.body: Eat a variety of colours every day.

fruits.title: Fruits
fruits.body: Full of vitamins, minerals and fibre.

protein.title: Fish & lean protein
protein.body: Fish 2–3 times a week if available; red meat only occasionally.

dairy.title: Low-fat dairy
dairy.body: A good source of calcium and protein.

salt.title: Salt
salt.body: No more than 5 g a day — about one teaspoon. Most salt comes from processed and packaged food.

processedMeat.title: Processed meats
processedMeat.body: High in salt and saturated fat.

redMeat.title: Red meat
redMeat.body: Limit lean red meat to 1–3 times a week.

sugar.title: Added sugar
sugar.body: Choose foods and drinks with no added sugar.

fullFatDairy.title: Full-fat dairy
fullFatDairy.body: With heart disease or high cholesterol, choose reduced-fat instead.
